card.name: Subject right before "cannot"
card.fires_on: The last word of a subject just before the verb "cannot" or "cannot be avoided", mostly in drug-label phrases like "if concomitant use cannot be avoided". It also fires on subjects in rule statements such as "A struct cannot inherit".

modes.label: Use or coadministration cannot be avoided
modes.description: The noun or word before "cannot be avoided" in drug interaction instructions.
modes.example: If concomitant<< use>> cannot be avoided, decrease the P-g

modes.label: Subject of a restriction
modes.description: A subject followed by "cannot" or "may not" in a rule or limitation, including programming text.
modes.example: A<< struct>> may not declare a default constructor

modes.label: Patients who cannot
modes.description: Words in a heading about people who cannot do something, such as swallow tablets.
modes.example: Administration of 20 mg Tablets to Patients<< Who>> Cannot Swallow Intact Tablets

card.writes: It pushes toward words meaning cannot or unable (Chinese 难, 無法) and away from "could" in several languages.
card.plain: It marks a spot where the next word is likely to be "cannot", as in "if use cannot be avoided".
